title: Court Attention at All Costs
summary: Everything is judged by its appearance; what is unseen counts for nothing. Never let yourself get lost in the crowd or buried in oblivion. Stand out, be seen, and court attention at all costs by being a magnet of curiosity, mystery, and notoriety, making yourself larger than life and more interesting than the mediocre.
example: P.T. Barnum used notoriety and curiosity to keep people intrigued and following his ventures.
Thomas Edison valued being in the public eye as much as his inventions, ensuring he received the credit and attention.
Mata Hari used an air of mystery, exotic costumes, and strategic reveals to captivate audiences and become famous despite not being the best dancer.
reversal: In the long run, excessive attention and cheap mystery can bore people or unravel into a perceived con, destroying your reputation.
Never grab attention away from a more powerful master or person in the room, as this can be seen as disrespect and lead to your downfall.
